title: Swing-point detector — non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's full review of PR #153 (backend-swing-point-detector), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: docs/architecture/Backend.md §2's module-layout tree wasn't updated to list the new app/signals/swing_points.py module under signals/, the same recurring gap already flagged (still unresolved) as a non-blocking follow-up on the prior backend-support-resistance PR (#147) for support_resistance.py. Add both to the tree in the same pass.

Plateau/tie merging (app/signals/swing_points.py's _merge_plateau_runs) collapses a run of identical-value bars to a SwingPoint at the run's middle bar, which shifts the reported extreme's date away from wherever it actually first/last occurred within the run. Very unlikely to matter for continuous float price/indicator series (an exact tie across multiple consecutive bars is rare outside synthetic data), but the future backend-divergence-detection task implements Kerry Lovvorn's empirical '20-40 bars apart' spacing rule (docs/ideas.md, MACD-Histogram divergence idea) off these dates -- that task should explicitly confirm the middle-bar convention doesn't distort spacing measurement (or note why it doesn't matter in practice) rather than silently inheriting the assumption.

Reuse: the task's decisions entry evaluated two alternatives for avoiding duplication with app.signals.support_resistance._find_swing_points (generalizing that function to accept a DataFrame-or-Series, and a scipy.signal.argrelextrema-based rewrite) and rejected both, but didn't consider a third, narrower option -- extracting just the low-level 'is bar i a local extreme over a full non-NaN window' comparison as a small shared primitive that both modules' genuinely different post-processing (support_resistance's high/low-vs-close touch selection; swing_points's plateau merging) could each layer on top of. Would remove ~15 lines of duplicated core-loop logic between the two modules without forcing either caller into the other's shape. Worth considering next time support_resistance.py is touched.

Minor efficiency: swing_highs() and swing_lows() (app/signals/swing_points.py) each independently run the full find_swing_points() pass (computing both kinds and merging plateau runs for both) and then filter by kind. A caller wanting both (plausible for a divergence detector) does the full pass twice. Trivial at typical daily-bar series lengths, but worth a shared-computation path if a hot-path caller ever needs both sides.

Style/efficiency: find_swing_points's core scan uses a manual Python loop with a fresh series.iloc[...] slice + .max()/.min()/.isna().any() per candidate bar (O(n*window)) instead of the vectorized centered-rolling idiom (series.rolling(2*window+1, center=True).max()/.min()) already used elsewhere in this codebase (e.g. app/indicators/stochastic.py, app/signals/engine.py). Not a correctness issue at typical daily-bar lengths, but makes this module the odd one out stylistically and the slower path over longer/intraday series.
